conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 53 years old, and I'm here because I've been having chest pain when I walk. It feels like pressure in my chest, and it's been going on for about three months. I haven't been able to keep up with my walking because of it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and describe the chest pain in more detail, including its location, duration, intensity, and any associated symptoms?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 53 years old, and I'm a female. The chest pain is in my chest, and it feels like pressure. It mainly happens when I'm walking, and it's been going on for about three months. It doesn't go away right away, and I haven't been able to keep up with my walking because of it. I don't have any other symptoms right now, like shortness of breath or sweating.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please provide details about your past medical history, including any previous illnesses, surgeries, or allergies?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't have any allergies, and I don't remember having any surgeries. I do have diabetes, and I was told I might have high blood pressure, but no one has given me medication for it yet. I'm on metformin for my diabetes.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please describe if the chest pain radiates to other areas, such as your arms, jaw, or back? Also, are there any specific activities or positions that make the pain worse or better?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The chest pain doesn't radiate anywhere else, just stays in my chest. It mainly happens when I'm walking, and it's been getting in the way of me keeping up with my walks. I haven't found anything that makes it better except maybe resting, but I haven't tried anything specific.
